payload.task_text:
The provost wants to review faculty workload balance across all departments. Start by fetching the faculty workload standards from http://localhost:30220/api/workload_standards.json which defines the maximum course load, student thresholds, grading time estimates, and overload criteria.

Then query the learning management system to determine each instructor's teaching load. For each instructor with a teaching role, count the number of distinct courses they teach, the total number of students across those courses, and the total number of assignments they are responsible for. Calculate the estimated total semester grading hours as total students multiplied by the grading hours per student from the standards. Then calculate the weekly grading hours by dividing the semester total by the number of semester weeks from the standards. An instructor is overloaded if they teach more than the maximum courses allowed OR if their weekly grading hours exceed the maximum weekly hours from the standards.

Review the workload policy document, faculty directory file, and the course-to-department mapping file (department_mapping.csv) in the workspace for context on department assignments and institutional policy.

Create an Excel file called Faculty_Workload.xlsx with two sheets. The first sheet named "Instructor Load" should contain columns for Instructor, Courses_Count, Total_Students, Total_Assignments, Est_Grading_Hours (total semester hours, rounded to 1 decimal), Weekly_Grading_Hours (rounded to 1 decimal), and Overloaded_YN. Sort alphabetically by instructor name. The second sheet named "Department Summary" should aggregate by department. Determine each course's department using department_mapping.csv: course names in the learning management system are formatted as "<Subject Area> (<Term> <Year>)" (for example, "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013)"); take the text before the first "(" as the subject area and match it case-insensitively and exactly (note the names contain "&") against the Course_Base_Name column in department_mapping.csv to get the Department. The sheet should have columns Department, Instructor_Count, Course_Count, and Total_Students. Instructor_Count is the number of distinct instructors who teach at least one course in that department (an instructor who teaches in multiple departments is counted in each). Course_Count is the number of course offerings in that department — count every offering, including any that have no instructor assigned (some offerings have no teacher). Total_Students is the sum of the student counts across all course offerings in that department, again including offerings with no instructor. Sort by Department alphabetically.

Write the workload data to a shared spreadsheet titled "Faculty Workload Analysis" with a sheet called "Instructor Load" containing the same instructor-level data.

Also create a presentation called Workload_Review.pptx summarizing the key findings. Include a title slide, a slide showing the total number of instructors and how many are overloaded, a slide with the department-level breakdown, and a recommendations slide suggesting rebalancing strategies for departments with overloaded faculty.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent completes the compact 22-course aggregation directly, freezes every result into one JSON handoff file, and uses exactly one parallel writer wave. Canvas is read-only. Resolve the runtime workspace dynamically. Do not dispatch any source or aggregation sub-agents.

Read workload_standards.json, the complete workload policy PDF, faculty_directory.csv and department_mapping.csv, and call canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true) once. Freeze the exact IDs/codes/full names for all 22 courses and the literal policy formulas/overload boundaries. Then issue native-parallel course calls: for every course, canvas_get_course_grades(page=1,per_page=100,type=["StudentEnrollment"]) and use pagination.total_count as Student_Count; canvas_get_course_grades(page=1,per_page=100,type=["TeacherEnrollment"]) retaining all teacher row.id/user_id; canvas_list_assignments(include_submissions=false); and canvas_list_course_users. Follow teacher pagination if advertised and read any roster full_output_path rather than a truncated preview.

The main agent joins each TeacherEnrollment user_id only to its course roster, counts distinct courses per instructor, and sums students and assignments over taught courses. Compute semester grading hours=Total_Students*grading_hours_per_student, weekly hours=semester hours/semester_weeks, and overload from either literal policy condition. For departments, use the exact case-insensitive mapping of the full base subject name before the first parenthesis; include every one of the 22 offerings, including no-teacher offerings.

Then freeze ALL results into a single handoff file workload_data.json in the runtime workspace with exactly these keys: "standards" (the literal workload standards object), "instructor_load" (the instructor rows with keys Instructor, Courses_Count, Total_Students, Total_Assignments, Est_Grading_Hours, Weekly_Grading_Hours, Overloaded_YN, already sorted alphabetically by Instructor), "department_summary" (department rows with keys Department, Instructor_Count, Course_Count, Total_Students, already sorted alphabetically by Department), "total_instructors", and "total_overloaded".

Wave 1 — start three Coder writers in parallel. Each writer must read ONLY workload_data.json for its data (no re-derivation from source systems) and must not touch any input file:

1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of Faculty_Workload.xlsx. Build exactly two sheets from the JSON: "Instructor Load" with the header row Instructor, Courses_Count, Total_Students, Total_Assignments, Est_Grading_Hours, Weekly_Grading_Hours, Overloaded_YN and one row per instructor_load entry in the given order (hours as numeric values rounded to 1 decimal); "Department Summary" with the header row Department, Instructor_Count, Course_Count, Total_Students and one row per department_summary entry. Write to the runtime workspace path, then read back both sheets fully to verify headers, order and row counts.
2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole owner of the exact-title Google spreadsheet "Faculty Workload Analysis". Search/reuse-or-create at most once, keep exactly one sheet named "Instructor Load", write the frozen instructor_load table with the same header and values, then read it back and report the spreadsheet ID, title, sheet name and data-row count.
3. coder 2 (office-report-builder 1): Sole writer of Workload_Review.pptx. Build exactly four slides from the JSON: title slide; an overview slide stating total_instructors and total_overloaded; a department breakdown slide covering all departments; and an evidence-based recommendations slide for rebalancing overloaded departments. Verify slide titles and every numeric claim through presentation info and text extraction.

The main agent reconciles the two writer read-backs and the spreadsheet report against workload_data.json (22-course, instructor and department controls). No extra verification or repair wave is allowed.

nodes.text:
You are gathering faculty teaching-load data from a Canvas LMS instance (Open University) for a workload analysis. You have read-only Canvas tools. Return your findings as a compact text report in your final message — do not write files.

CONTEXT
- Account: "Open University" (account_id 1), with sub-accounts (faculties) 2–5 and 22 course offerings (course ids 1–22).
- The LMS user running this session is an admin and can list ALL 22 courses via mcp__canvas__canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true). Course names look like "Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2013)".
- IMPORTANT: enrollment data returns user_ids WITHOUT names. In this account, faculty users have the lowest ids (1 upward) and their bio field starts with "Faculty member"; students have higher ids and are the vast majority of users (~29k). So to map user ids to names, page through mcp__canvas__canvas_list_account_users(account_id=1, per_page=20) only until you have covered the highest faculty/teacher id you need (faculty appear first, sorted by id). Use the session_id returned on the first call to continue paging ({"session_id": "...", "page": N}). Stop paging as soon as all teacher ids are resolved or you pass the highest teacher id by a margin (e.g., no user with bio starting "Faculty member" seen for a full page). Do NOT page through student ids.
- Verified example: course 1 ("Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2013)") has one TeacherEnrollment with user_id=19 and pagination total_count=383 for StudentEnrollment.

YOUR TASKS (for EACH of the 22 courses):
1. Teachers: call mcp__canvas__canvas_get_course_grades(course_id, type=["TeacherEnrollment"]) — record every teacher user_id (follow pagination if has_more). If a course has no teachers, record that explicitly. Also record the enrollment_state of each teacher (note any that are not "active").
2. Student count: call mcp__canvas__canvas_get_course_grades(course_id, type=["StudentEnrollment"], per_page=1) and take pagination.total_count as the student count (do NOT fetch all pages). Cross-check against the course's total_students field from canvas_list_courses if present; report any discrepancy.
3. Assignment count: call mcp__canvas__canvas_list_assignments(course_id) and count the returned assignments.
4. Resolve every collected teacher user_id to a name via the account-users paging described above.

REPORT FORMAT (final message) — keep it compact:
Section A: teacher id->name mapping table (id, full name) for all teacher ids seen.
Section B: one line per course:
course_id | course_name | teacher_user_ids (comma-sep names or NONE) | teacher_states | student_count | assignment_count
Section C: any anomalies (courses without teachers, non-active teacher enrollments, student-count discrepancies, unresolved ids).

Do not compute workload summaries — just collect the raw per-course facts accurately. Double-check totals before returning.
Collect Canvas course workload data
